---
title: "Defining trips from vessel tracks"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

A trip (voyage) is the part of a vessel track between leaving port and
returning to port. In ramb, cutting a track into trips is step 1 of the
fishing-activity flow, done by `rb_cut_trip_voyages()`. One function, three
rules (`method`): here we compare two of them on the Danish example data.

## Pings in port and at sea

First, flag each ping as in port or at sea. `dansk_harbours` is a set of
harbour polygons shipped with the package; `rb_detect_in_polygons()` tells
us which pings fall inside one. Trips are cut on `port_id`: a value in port,
`NA` at sea.

```{r}
library(ramb)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

d <-
  dansk |>
  arrange(vessel_id, time_stamp) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    in_harbour = rb_detect_in_polygons(geometry, dansk_harbours),
    port_id = if_else(in_harbour, 1L, NA_integer_)
  ) |>
  st_drop_geometry()
```

## Two cutting rules

* `method = "runs"`: every run of pings in port, however short, ends a
  voyage.
* `method = "jepol"`: the ICES VMS datacall rule (`define_trips_pol`). A
  voyage runs from the first ping at sea to the first ping back in port;
  voyages shorter than `min_dur_h` hours are dropped, and voyages longer
  than `max_dur_h` hours are split at long gaps between pings.

The ping columns are called `vessel_id` and `time_stamp` in `dansk`, so we
say so via `vid` and `time`:

```{r}
jepol <- rb_cut_trip_voyages(d, method = "jepol", vid = vessel_id, time = time_stamp)
runs  <- rb_cut_trip_voyages(d, method = "runs",  vid = vessel_id, time = time_stamp)
```

Both return one row per voyage: vessel, year, voyage id, start and end time,
the ports departed from and returned to, and the number of pings.

```{r}
jepol
```

## Comparison

The two rules largely agree on these data; the jepol rule drops a few short
harbour-to-harbour runs:

```{r}
count(jepol, vessel_id, name = "voyages_jepol") |>
  full_join(count(runs, vessel_id, name = "voyages_runs"), by = "vessel_id")
```

A third rule, `method = "stays"`, cuts the track at port *stays* found by
`rb_find_trip_stays()` — stays being longer stops, so brief harbour passages
do not end a voyage. That is the rule used in the full fishing-activity
flow.
